title: The Last Séance at Ravenmoor
setting: Ravenmoor Manor — a crumbling stone estate on the fog-choked moors. Tonight is the first anniversary of Lady Eleanor Ravenmoor's death. A storm has washed out the only road. No one leaves until dawn. Content notes: poisoning, an off-screen death and a staged séance. No graphic descriptions.
intro:
You have been summoned to Ravenmoor Manor by Lord Ambrose Ravenmoor. One year ago tonight, his young wife Eleanor died of a sudden "fever." Now Ambrose has hired a famous medium to call her back from the grave.

The storm has swallowed the road. The candles are lit around the séance table. The clock in the hall is creeping toward midnight.

Something in this house is listening.

Tonight's three guests carry the investigation themselves. Their observations and the records read at the table are public; nobody needs a hidden packet or an extra actor.

Other named people are part of the supplied accounts, not extra players. The host reads their evidence aloud. The physician, butler and sister remain the locked master cast.

victim.name: Lord Ambrose Ravenmoor
victim.description: Master of Ravenmoor Manor. Grieving, obsessive, and lately convinced that his wife Eleanor did not die of fever at all.

rounds.title: Round 1 - The Glass in the Dark
rounds.narration:
Midnight strikes. Madame Vesper presses her concealed pedal; the candles die. A chair scrapes beside Dr. Ashgrove. Someone reaches across the table. A choking sound, then breaking glass. When the candles return, Ambrose is dead, his lips blue. Ashgrove is already beside him and calls it a weak heart.

Constance poured the brandy before the seance. Her own drink came from the same decanter. Crane was in the doorway during the darkness, returning to pocket a silver candlestick. Those are movements to investigate, not verdicts. Nobody may leave the stormbound manor.

Read the first observations aloud. Separate what somebody did tonight from what they stood to gain. A debt can explain resentment; it cannot identify the hand at the glass.

The host reads the supplied character accounts verbatim; players need no absent actor:
Dr. Silas Ashgrove: "I saw Madame Vesper Thorne press a hidden pedal just before the lights died. Then a hand reached and someone choked. I want that darkness explained."
Hollis Crane: "I saw Lady Constance Ravenmoor pour brandy before the candles failed; she drank from that decanter too. Ambrose died beside shattered glass. I wonder who touched his alone."
Lady Constance Ravenmoor: "I read Ambrose's letter threatening to report Father Lucan Grey's drinking to the bishop; he objects to our seance. I hear a grievance, but how does it explain that glass and blackout?"
Madame Vesper Thorne: "I learned Hollis Crane returned to the doorway in the blackout to pocket a silver candlestick. That explains movement when Ambrose died. I still wonder whether he approached the glass."
Father Lucan Grey: "I heard the chair beside Dr. Silas Ashgrove scrape; a hand reached toward Ambrose. Light returns; he's at the body, calling blue lips 'weak heart.' I can't reconcile choking and shattered glass."

rounds.title: Round 2 - The Bottle and the Wire
rounds.narration:
Three knocks sound beneath the table. A wire catches the candlelight. The spirit board spells TONIC, but the mechanism, not a ghost, moved it. Ambrose hired Vesper to stage a performance; the script has not yet been examined.

A servant brings down Eleanor's old tonic bottle, kept at Ambrose's request for the constable. Its label bears S.A. in Ashgrove's handwriting. In the conservatory, monkshood stems have been freshly cut; soil leads toward the physician's chair. Monkshood is also called wolfsbane. Its poison can produce the symptoms seen on Ambrose.

Accounts, letters and household complaints now expose the disputes surrounding tonight: Constance's gambling debt, Crane's stolen silver, and Vesper's threatened exposure as a fraud. The bottle links the present investigation to Eleanor's death a year ago. It does not yet show how tonight's poison reached the victim.

The host reads the supplied character accounts verbatim; players need no absent actor:
Dr. Silas Ashgrove: "I learned Eleanor told Father Lucan Grey she feared her medicine; he never warned us. His silence protected someone while she worsened. I'm worried."
Hollis Crane: "I found a wire beneath the table linking Madame Vesper Thorne to those spirit knocks. Ambrose threatened to expose her fraud. I wonder what she'd do to silence him."
Lady Constance Ravenmoor: "I see stolen silver linking Hollis Crane to secret dealings outside the manor. He knows the drinks, and his livelihood's threatened. After that tonic discovery, I'm uneasy."
Madame Vesper Thorne: "I found initials on Eleanor's old tonic bottle. I recognize S.A. in Dr. Silas Ashgrove's handwriting; cut-monkshood soil leads toward his chair. I wonder if it's the same poison twice."
Father Lucan Grey: "I learned Lady Constance Ravenmoor hid gambling debts; Ambrose refused her money at dinner. Her inheritance would settle them. I wonder whether pouring those drinks was more than hospitality."

rounds.title: Round 4 - What Eleanor Left Behind
rounds.narration:
Eleanor's preserved correspondence describes numb lips after her nightly medicine and plants dying when she poured it into their pots. Her diary says, "S. knows that I know. He watches me drink every night." With the letters is an account of false prescriptions and two patients who died. Eleanor had intended to tell Ambrose. Ashgrove signed her death certificate as fever.

Ambrose's written instructions to the medium are found: ask, "Who gave me the tonic?" He paid for a trap, not a genuine spirit. A note from his coat says, "Watch S.A.'s hands when the lights return." The withheld codicil directs attention to the signer of Eleanor's death certificate. The records are now on the table for these guests to compare.

Now read the new clues. Documents supply a reason to fear this gathering. The final task is still to connect that fear to the movements around Ambrose's glass.

The host reads the supplied character accounts verbatim; players need no absent actor:
Dr. Silas Ashgrove: "I heard Lady Constance Ravenmoor wish Ambrose would join Eleanor during their dinner argument. With her gambling debts and those poured drinks, I can't dismiss that resentment."
Hollis Crane: "I read Dr. Silas Ashgrove's fever certificate, but Eleanor's discarded tonic numbed her lips and killed plants. His bottle initials worry me. I want that medicine explained."
Lady Constance Ravenmoor: "I learned Madame Vesper Thorne was paid triple for Ambrose's script and controlled the bellows. With exposure threatened too, I can't call that staged darkness harmless entertainment."
Madame Vesper Thorne: "I learned Father Lucan Grey heard Eleanor say medicine, not fever, would kill her. He stayed silent when Ambrose demanded justice. I wonder whether he's protecting a confession or a person."
Father Lucan Grey: "I learned Hollis Crane returned to pocket a candlestick in the seance room. That puts him in the doorway during darkness. I can't ignore movement while Ambrose's glass was within reach."

rounds.title: Round 5 - The Drink That Did Not Kill
rounds.narration:
The remaining brandy and the fragments of Ambrose's glass are compared. The decanter has no wolfsbane residue; the individual glass rim does. Constance drank from the same decanter and survived. Pouring the drinks is not the same as touching one rim during the blackout.

The doorway account describes a serpent-and-staff ring on the reaching hand. Ashgrove wears that physician's ring. The doorway account is recorded beside the glass findings. Its description of a ring should be tested against the poison evidence and the movements in the dark. The medium's script explains the false haunting. It does not explain the poisoned glass. The stolen candlestick explains Crane's doorway movement without making him an innocent witness by decree.

Keep the earlier accusations beside these corrections. Ask which explanation fits the bottle, the shared drink and the single poisoned rim without changing any of those facts.

The host reads the supplied character accounts verbatim; players need no absent actor:
Dr. Silas Ashgrove: "I know Hollis Crane noticed Eleanor's tonic bottle and the glass evidence. I see why he'd hide stolen silver, but that clean decanter leaves Ambrose's poisoned rim unexplained."
Hollis Crane: "I learned Father Lucan Grey kept Eleanor's warning under confession's seal. She said medicine, not fever, would kill her. I understand silence, but I still want the tonic checked."
Lady Constance Ravenmoor: "I heard Dr. Silas Ashgrove call it a weak heart despite recognizing poison symptoms. The clean decanter points to Ambrose's glass. With his old tonic and that scripted question, I'm not convinced."
Madame Vesper Thorne: "I saw Lady Constance Ravenmoor drink from that decanter and survive; poison was on Ambrose's glass alone. Her inheritance troubles me, but pouring isn't proof."
Father Lucan Grey: "I read Ambrose's paid script telling Madame Vesper Thorne to ask, "Who gave me the tonic?" I see a planned trap behind her hidden fraud, not proof of supernatural murder."

rounds.title: Round 7 - The Hand at the Glass
rounds.narration:
Place the evidence in order. Before tonight, Eleanor recorded harm from medicine and threatened to expose the prescription accounts. Tonight Ambrose brought the bottle and hired the performance to ask about it. During the blackout, a chair scraped, a ringed hand reached toward his glass, and he died. The poison was on that glass alone.

The final comparison adds the glove observation: Ashgrove removed his gloves before the seance and replaced them when the lights returned. It is a witness detail to test against the ring account, not a confession. His immediate weak-heart explanation must also be weighed against the poison symptoms, handwriting and soil.

Read every final clue. Other guests have debts and wrongdoing, but do those explain both deaths and this method? Name a suspect from the evidence already spoken, not from a secret packet or a supernatural answer.

The host reads the supplied character accounts verbatim; players need no absent actor:
Dr. Silas Ashgrove: "I know Madame Vesper Thorne hid a fraud. Ambrose knowingly hired it to ask about the tonic, but died before that question. I still wonder who poisoned his glass in her darkness."
Hollis Crane: "I know Lady Constance Ravenmoor inherits, but her shared drink was harmless. Pouring isn't touching Ambrose's rim in darkness. Her account of Eleanor's numb lips makes me worry about that tonic."
Lady Constance Ravenmoor: "I know Father Lucan Grey withheld a warning from before tonight's murder; it points to the tonic. Threatened exposure of his drinking doesn't explain the poisoned rim or ring to me."
Madame Vesper Thorne: "I place Hollis Crane in the doorway; the candlestick explains his presence, not both deaths. That serpent-and-staff ring description and poison on Ambrose's glass still need explaining to me."
Father Lucan Grey: "I recognize Dr. Silas Ashgrove's serpent-and-staff ring on that reaching hand; wolfsbane coats Ambrose's rim, not the decanter. Bottle and soil link both deaths. I doubt Dr. Silas Ashgrove's 'weak heart'; Eleanor's tonic question threatens him."

The clock strikes three. The candles gutter low.

solution.explanation: Ashgrove is the only suspect connecting both deaths. Eleanor's preserved papers describe harmful tonic, false prescriptions and her intention to expose them; his handwriting is on the bottle and he certified fever. Ambrose kept those records and hired a staged seance to ask about the tonic. During its blackout, the account of a reaching hand identifies the physician's serpent-and-staff ring. The poison was on Ambrose's glass rim, not in the decanter Constance drank from. The cut monkshood, soil and glove observation corroborate the method and opportunity. Debts, thefts and the fraudulent performance explain other suspicious acts, but not this whole chain. No supernatural confession or private clue is needed.
solution.revealNarration: The room returns to the records and observations it heard aloud. The murderer is Dr. Silas Ashgrove. No confession is needed: the public evidence tells the story.

readAloud.contradictingDetail: Ambrose threatened to expose her fraud. I wonder what she'd do to silence him.

readAloud.text: I read {ashgrove}'s fever certificate, but Eleanor's discarded tonic numbed her lips and killed plants. His bottle initials worry me. I want that medicine explained.
readAloud.observation: I read {ashgrove}'s fever certificate, but Eleanor's discarded tonic numbed her lips and killed plants.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: His bottle initials worry me. I want that medicine explained.

readAloud.text: I learned {grey} kept Eleanor's warning under confession's seal. She said medicine, not fever, would kill her. I understand silence, but I still want the tonic checked.
readAloud.observation: I learned {grey} kept Eleanor's warning under confession's seal.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: She said medicine, not fever, would kill her. I understand silence, but I still want the tonic checked.

readAloud.text: I know {constance} inherits, but her shared drink was harmless. Pouring isn't touching Ambrose's rim in darkness. Her account of Eleanor's numb lips makes me worry about that tonic.
readAloud.observation: I know {constance} inherits, but her shared drink was harmless.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Pouring isn't touching Ambrose's rim in darkness. Her account of Eleanor's numb lips makes me worry about that tonic.

readAloud.text: I read Ambrose's letter threatening to report {grey}'s drinking to the bishop; he objects to our seance. I hear a grievance, but how does it explain that glass and blackout?
readAloud.observation: I read Ambrose's letter threatening to report {grey}'s drinking to the bishop; he objects to our seance.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I hear a grievance, but how does it explain that glass and blackout?

readAloud.text: I see stolen silver linking {crane} to secret dealings outside the manor. He knows the drinks, and his livelihood's threatened. After that tonic discovery, I'm uneasy.
readAloud.observation: I see stolen silver linking {crane} to secret dealings outside the manor.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: He knows the drinks, and his livelihood's threatened. After that tonic discovery, I'm uneasy.

readAloud.text: I learned {vesper} was paid triple for Ambrose's script and controlled the bellows. With exposure threatened too, I can't call that staged darkness harmless entertainment.
readAloud.observation: I learned {vesper} was paid triple for Ambrose's script and controlled the bellows.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: With exposure threatened too, I can't call that staged darkness harmless entertainment.

readAloud.text: I heard {ashgrove} call it a weak heart despite recognizing poison symptoms. The clean decanter points to Ambrose's glass. With his old tonic and that scripted question, I'm not convinced.
readAloud.observation: I heard {ashgrove} call it a weak heart despite recognizing poison symptoms.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The clean decanter points to Ambrose's glass. With his old tonic and that scripted question, I'm not convinced.

readAloud.text: I know {grey} withheld a warning from before tonight's murder; it points to the tonic. Threatened exposure of his drinking doesn't explain the poisoned rim or ring to me.
readAloud.observation: I know {grey} withheld a warning from before tonight's murder; it points to the tonic.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Threatened exposure of his drinking doesn't explain the poisoned rim or ring to me.

readAloud.text: I learned {crane} returned to the doorway in the blackout to pocket a silver candlestick. That explains movement when Ambrose died. I still wonder whether he approached the glass.
readAloud.observation: I learned {crane} returned to the doorway in the blackout to pocket a silver candlestick.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: That explains movement when Ambrose died. I still wonder whether he approached the glass.

readAloud.text: I found initials on Eleanor's old tonic bottle. I recognize S.A. in {ashgrove}'s handwriting; cut-monkshood soil leads toward his chair. I wonder if it's the same poison twice.
readAloud.observation: I found initials on Eleanor's old tonic bottle.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I recognize S.A. in {ashgrove}'s handwriting; cut-monkshood soil leads toward his chair. I wonder if it's the same poison twice.

readAloud.text: I learned {grey} heard Eleanor say medicine, not fever, would kill her. He stayed silent when Ambrose demanded justice. I wonder whether he's protecting a confession or a person.
readAloud.observation: I learned {grey} heard Eleanor say medicine, not fever, would kill her.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: He stayed silent when Ambrose demanded justice. I wonder whether he's protecting a confession or a person.

readAloud.text: I saw {constance} drink from that decanter and survive; poison was on Ambrose's glass alone. Her inheritance troubles me, but pouring isn't proof.
readAloud.observation: I saw {constance} drink from that decanter and survive; poison was on Ambrose's glass alone.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Her inheritance troubles me, but pouring isn't proof.

readAloud.text: I place {crane} in the doorway; the candlestick explains his presence, not both deaths. That serpent-and-staff ring description and poison on Ambrose's glass still need explaining to me.
readAloud.observation: I place {crane} in the doorway; the candlestick explains his presence, not both deaths.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: That serpent-and-staff ring description and poison on Ambrose's glass still need explaining to me.

readAloud.text: I heard the chair beside {ashgrove} scrape; a hand reached toward Ambrose. Light returns; he's at the body, calling blue lips 'weak heart.' I can't reconcile choking and shattered glass.
readAloud.observation: I heard the chair beside {ashgrove} scrape; a hand reached toward Ambrose.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Light returns; he's at the body, calling blue lips 'weak heart.' I can't reconcile choking and shattered glass.

readAloud.text: I learned {constance} hid gambling debts; Ambrose refused her money at dinner. Her inheritance would settle them. I wonder whether pouring those drinks was more than hospitality.
readAloud.observation: I learned {constance} hid gambling debts; Ambrose refused her money at dinner.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Her inheritance would settle them. I wonder whether pouring those drinks was more than hospitality.

readAloud.text: I learned {crane} returned to pocket a candlestick in the seance room. That puts him in the doorway during darkness. I can't ignore movement while Ambrose's glass was within reach.
readAloud.observation: I learned {crane} returned to pocket a candlestick in the seance room.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: That puts him in the doorway during darkness. I can't ignore movement while Ambrose's glass was within reach.

readAloud.text: I read Ambrose's paid script telling {vesper} to ask, "Who gave me the tonic?" I see a planned trap behind her hidden fraud, not proof of supernatural murder.
readAloud.observation: I read Ambrose's paid script telling {vesper} to ask, "Who gave me the tonic?"
readAloud.contradictingDetail: I see a planned trap behind her hidden fraud, not proof of supernatural murder.

readAloud.text: I recognize {ashgrove}'s serpent-and-staff ring on that reaching hand; wolfsbane coats Ambrose's rim, not the decanter. Bottle and soil link both deaths. I doubt {ashgrove}'s 'weak heart'; Eleanor's tonic question threatens him.
readAloud.observation: I recognize {ashgrove}'s serpent-and-staff ring on that reaching hand; wolfsbane coats Ambrose's rim, not the decanter.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Bottle and soil link both deaths. I doubt {ashgrove}'s 'weak heart'; Eleanor's tonic question threatens him.
